title: Pull Up Field

solutions.title: insuredValueCents lives on Instrument
solutions.tradeoff: Instrument's constructor grows a third parameter every subclass must thread through, and a future instrument category that genuinely carries no insured value - a loaner practice kazoo, say - inherits a field it cannot opt out of.

reviewFocus: Is insuredValueCents declared and assigned in exactly one place - Instrument's constructor - or does one subclass still redeclare it alongside the inherited copy?

Did gradeLevel get pulled up along with insuredValueCents because the two happened to share a declaration style? WindInstrument.gradeLevel and StringInstrument.gradeLevel are read by isSuitableFor and restorationCostMultiplier respectively - does the walkthrough show those two call sites disagree about what the number means, not just that the names match?
Does monthlyInsurancePremiumCents still type its parameter as the WindInstrument | StringInstrument union, or did it quietly narrow to a single subclass and stop compiling for the other?

Compare against drill-12-05: that drill pulls a field out of a shared base rather than into one. Does this walkthrough's test for 'is it really the same field' - matching usage, not matching name - actually hold up against 12-05's field, or is it only argued in one direction?

If WindInstrument and StringInstrument disagreed on the insurance rate itself (one insured at 0.4%, one at 0.6%), would insuredValueCents still be safe to pull up? Does the walkthrough say why the rate living outside both classes is what makes this safe?
